Subject: FYI: Forecast category clarifications + optional walkthrough (Apr 21)

Team —

Finance ran the usual pre-commit sanity pass and we hit a few recurring category mismatches that make weekly commit / best-case numbers noisy. To reduce variance and make monthly forecasting reviews actionable, finance is pushing an updated definitions doc and a short training session for sellers.

High level changes we want everyone to adopt starting Apr 26 (details in attached):
- Commit (aka "Forecast Commit"): only opportunities with signed PO/Procurement intent OR verbal purchase commitment + confirmed implementation window within 30 days. No pipeline-stage guesses.
- Best Case: opportunities with strong buying signal and an identified champion, but missing a signed PO; include a target close month and a realistic gating action.
- Pipeline: all other open opportunities that have not reached Best Case criteria.

Please review the attached "Forecast_Definitions_v2.pdf" before the session. We'll run a 30-minute walkthrough and a Q&A on Wed Apr 21 at 11:00 PT. Join link: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/832145227

Action items for sales leaders:
- Update open opportunities in SFDC that you own to the new categories by EOD Apr 25.
- Flag any accounts where you think the classification will change revenue recognition timing significantly — finance will follow up.

Marissa — I know you own a couple of larger deals with Northstar Health. If you want, we can do a 10-min slot in that session for their specific case (they asked about how proof-of-concept credits affect commit).

Thanks,
Karthik
--

Thanks Marissa — good questions. Quick answers below and we'll cover in the walkthrough.

1) Verbal commitments: please set the Opportunity Stage to "Commit" and add a one-line note in the new "Finance Commit Flag" checkbox + a short note in the Opportunity Comments field with the name of the buyer and the date of the verbal confirmation. If your CRM doesn't have the checkbox, set stage + put "VerbalCommit: <date> by <person>" in the comments. Finance will pick this up for the weekly rollup.

2) PoC credits: treat credits as an adjustment to the expected ACV for the first billed period. For forecasting, mark the opportunity as Commit if the procurement intent is clear and implementation window is inside 30 days — but in the notes, include the expected credit line and magnitude (we'll net it in ARR recognition). If credits are material (>10% of deal value) flag it explicitly and finance will run the adjusted recognition in the weekly model.

3) We'll record and post the session. Recording + the slide deck will be uploaded to the Sales Enablement folder after the call.

Marissa — for NSH specifically: if procurement review starts Apr 23 and Emily gives positive signals by Apr 24, you can move to Commit and include "ProcStart: 2026-04-23" in the comments. Finance will treat commit dated in the week ending Apr 25 as part of the Apr monthly commit.

Appreciate you attaching the snapshot — that's helpful. We'll follow up if we need numbers adjusted.

On Wed we'll also run a 10-minute live example with one real opportunity so sellers see how to mark things in SFDC. If you'd like NSH to be the example, say the word and I'll slot it in.

-Karthik
